findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "implementation", "behavior").
findings.evidence: Test behavior the user sees (roles, text), not implementation details (state, class names, internal calls)
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The setup commands omit packages the examples depend on, so the shown tests will not run as installed.
findings.evidence: Vitest install: "npm i -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react"; Jest install: "npm i -D jest jest-environment-jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom"; example uses userEvent.setup() and toBeInTheDocument()
findings.fix: Add @testing-library/dom (a peer dependency of RTL v16) to both installs. Add @testing-library/user-event to both. Add @testing-library/jest-dom to the Vitest install and import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest' in a setup file.

findings.summary: The setup table never installs @testing-library/user-event, and the Vitest column never installs @testing-library/jest-dom, yet the page's example test uses both.
findings.evidence: Install row: "npm i -D jest jest-environment-jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom" / "npm i -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react"; the example calls userEvent.setup() and toBeInTheDocument().
findings.fix: Add @testing-library/user-event to both install commands. Add @testing-library/jest-dom to the Vitest command, and note that the Vitest setup file must import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'.
